table.name: atom
table.purpose: One row per atom in a chemical structure database: each atom belongs to a molecule (444 molecules, ~500 total atoms each on average), is identified by a code combining the molecule id and a per-molecule atom number, and carries its chemical element symbol. Atom-to-atom connections are recorded in the 'connected' table.

atom_id.name: atom_id
atom_id.description: Primary key. Code of the form <molecule_id>_<atom_number>, e.g. TR024_11 = atom 11 of molecule TR024. Referenced by connected.atom_id and connected.atom_id2, which record bonds between atoms.

element.name: element
element.description: Chemical element symbol of the atom, lowercase (h, c, o, n, cl, br, si, p, zn, ...). 21 distinct elements; hydrogen and carbon dominate, consistent with organic molecules.

molecule_id.name: molecule_id
molecule_id.description: Foreign key to molecule.molecule_id; the molecule this atom belongs to. Matches the prefix of atom_id.

table.name: bond
table.purpose: Chemical bonds between atoms within molecules; each row is one bond in a molecule, identified by the molecule and the two atom indices it connects (e.g. TR031_18_36 = molecule TR031, atoms 18 and 36). Bond order is encoded in bond_type using standard chemical notation: '-' single, '=' double, '#' triple. Referenced by the 'connected' table, which presumably lists atom pairs per bond.

bond_id.name: bond_id
bond_id.description: Primary key. Composite code: molecule_id plus the two atom indices joined by the bond (e.g. TR031_18_36 = bond between atoms 18 and 36 of molecule TR031).

bond_type.name: bond_type
bond_type.description: Bond order in chemical notation: '-' single bond (10528), '=' double bond (1844), '#' triple bond (6).

molecule_id.name: molecule_id
molecule_id.description: Foreign key to molecule.molecule_id; the molecule containing this bond. 444 distinct molecules.

table.name: connected
table.purpose: Junction/edge table linking pairs of atoms to the bond between them; each row states that two atoms (atom_id, atom_id2) are connected via a given bond (bond_id). Bond IDs appear to be composed as <molecule>_<atom1>_<atom2> (e.g. TR018_11_12), and atom IDs as <molecule>_<atom index> (e.g. TR018_11). The ~0.5 uniqueness on bond_id suggests some bonds are recorded in both directions (a-b and b-a).

atom_id.name: atom_id
atom_id.description: Identifier of the first atom in the connected pair; references atom.atom_id. Format <molecule code>_<atom index> (e.g. TR018_11).

atom_id2.name: atom_id2
atom_id2.description: Identifier of the second atom in the connected pair; references atom.atom_id. Same format as atom_id.

bond_id.name: bond_id
bond_id.description: Identifier of the bond connecting the two atoms; references bond.bond_id. Format <molecule code>_<atom1 index>_<atom2 index> (e.g. TR018_11_12).

table.name: molecule
table.purpose: Registry of molecules, each identified by a code (TR###), with a binary class label. Atoms and bonds of each molecule are stored in the atom and bond tables referencing molecule_id. Likely a machine-learning dataset (e.g., mutagenicity classification) of labeled molecular graphs.

label.name: class_label
label.description: Binary class label of the molecule, encoded as '-' (191 molecules) and '+' (152 molecules). The exact semantic of the classes (e.g., positive/negative in a classification task such as mutagenicity or toxicity) is not determinable from the data alone; the '+'/'-' encoding strongly suggests a two-class target variable. No joined columns provide further evidence, so this reading remains plausible but unconfirmed.

molecule_id.name: molecule_id
molecule_id.description: Primary key. Unique identifier of a molecule, formatted as 'TR' followed by a zero-padded number (TR000–TR477 range observed). Referenced by atom.molecule_id and bond.molecule_id, which store the atoms and bonds belonging to each molecule.
